objective: Produce a first-wave row for approved support guidance lookup.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: The first wave is the set of use cases that go into Day-in-the-Life interviews and, later, the executive case. Each needs enough detail to be owned, measured, and tested.
What each first-wave use case needs

items: **A business owner and a technical owner.**
**A metric and baseline plan:** what will be measured, where, and over what period.
**Dependencies:** connectors, permissions, content quality, and actions.

blocks.x: A simple matrix is usually enough for live alignment. Glean's Value Playbook also provides an eight-dimension scoring model that covers factors such as business value potential, measurability, time to value, and cross-functional applicability. This can help expose differences between close candidates.

blocks.label: Caution
blocks.x: The playbook's scoring model rates some complexity dimensions so that a higher score is better. Interpret those dimensions carefully before adding scores together. Don't turn the raw total into an automated feasibility gate. This course uses explicit rationale and human review.
A first-wave use case is ready for DITL when every field below is filled in or explicitly marked unknown.

practice.x: Write a first-wave row for "approved support guidance lookup" in the fictional support scenario.

items: **Business owner:** support operations director. **Technical owner:** knowledge-base and platform owner.
**Data:** the approved knowledge base and past case resolutions. Assumption: agents' permissions mirror the knowledge-base groups, to be confirmed.
**Metric plan:** handle time for an agreed case class from the ticketing system, plus a resolution-quality guardrail and an agreed baseline window.
**DITL:** two tier 1 agents and one team lead, with dates booked.
**Risks:** article currency and ownership; content that lives only in team chat.
